title: Cross Modal Predictive Architecture for Material Property Prediction
experiments_summary: The study implements X-MoPA, a multimodal self-supervised framework integrating three encoders: CGCNN for crystal graph embeddings (atoms as nodes with physicochemical features, bonds as edges), MatSciBERT for text embeddings (template-generated structural descriptions from CIF files, encoded via a 12-layer BERT transformer, projected to 150-dimensional vectors), and a 1D CNN for XRD spectral embeddings (simulated via Pymatgen over 2θ range 5–90°, discretized into fixed-length arrays). The three modality-specific embeddings are projected into a shared latent space, where lightweight MLP predictors perform cross-modal prediction: for each training instance, two modalities are used to predict the latent representation of the third. The training objective combines a cross-modal MSE prediction loss (L2 norm between predicted and actual latent representations), a VICReg regularizer (variance, invariance, and covariance terms to prevent representational collapse), and a temperature-scaled InfoNCE contrastive loss (positive pairs from different modalities of the same instance, negatives from different instances). The model is trained with AdamW optimizer and cosine annealing scheduler on an NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU using PyTorch. Experiments are conducted on the Matbench benchmark suite focusing on 5 crystal property regression tasks with predefined 5-fold train-test splits. Downstream evaluation uses fine-tuning of only the final prediction heads (0.6% of parameters) while keeping encoder weights frozen. Additional evaluation is performed on the AFLOW database (~60,000 materials) with an 80/10/10 train/validation/test split for pretraining, followed by fine-tuning on a 5,000-sample subset for band gap prediction. Performance is compared against CGCNN, ALIGNN, and CoGCNN using mean absolute error (MAE), with baseline results taken from the official Matbench leaderboard.
